q: Why can money and a document also be called 'ways', though the word suits only *bi'ah*?
options: They too exist for the sake of the marital union
They were once the same act
The Torah calls all three 'ways' explicitly
They are learned from Efron's field
why: Money and document also serve *bi'ah*, the purpose of betrothal, so the Mishnah uses one word for all three.

q: In R. Shimon's parable, why is it the man who 'takes' a woman?
options: As an owner searches for his lost item: woman was formed from man's side
Because the man pays the money
Because men decide when to marry
Because the father hands her over
why: The one who lost something seeks it, not the reverse; so it is a man's way to pursue a woman.

q: What general rule does the Gemara finally adopt for when a Mishnah says 'ways' rather than 'matters'?
options: 'Ways' where there is a distinction, 'matters' where there is none
'Ways' for Torah law, 'matters' for rabbinic law
'Ways' for women, 'matters' for men
'Ways' for natural processes only
why: Proven from R. Eliezer, who says the *etrog* is like a tree 'in every matter', with no distinction.

q: According to the first answer, what does the number in 'three ways' exclude?
options: *Chuppah*
*Chalipin*
*Chalitzah*
*Yichud*
why: The wedding canopy does not effect betrothal; for Rav Huna, who holds *chuppah* acquires, it excludes *chalipin* instead.

options: It works even with an item worth less than a *perutah*
It requires a written document
It can only acquire land
It needs the woman to give something
why: A woman does not give herself over for less than a *perutah*; Rashi calls it demeaning, Tosafot say it shows *chalipin* is not *kesef*.

q: How do Rashi and Tosafot differ on why *chalipin* fails?
options: Rashi: it demeans her; Tosafot: it is a different instrument from *kesef*
Rashi: it is too cheap; Tosafot: it needs witnesses
Rashi: it is rabbinic; Tosafot: it is biblical
They agree completely
why: For Rashi the problem is dignity (*genai hu lah*); for Tosafot, classification: *chalipin* works by the object, *kesef* by value.

q: Why can't *chalitzah* free a married woman, despite the *kal va'chomer* from the *yevamah*?
options: The verse says 'a scroll of severance': only a document severs her
Because she was never a *yevamah*
Because *chalitzah* is rabbinic
Because only death frees a married woman
why: *Sefer keritut* (Devarim 24:3) teaches that a document, and nothing else, ends the marriage.

q: Whose is the betrothal money of a *na'arah* (a girl between twelve and twelve and a half)?
options: Her father's
Her own
Her mother's
It is returned to the groom
why: "In her youth, in her father's house" (Bamidbar 30:17): her gains in her youth belong to her father.
